content_blocks.text: Overview
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus
Overview

content_blocks.text: The PPN applies to central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies, and to best value authorities within the meaning of section 1 of the Local Government Act 1999 (c. 27) and parish councils in England (collectively referred to as ‘in-scope organisations’).
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus
Overview

content_blocks.text: For all new procurements, in-scope organisations can decline to consider (or otherwise exclude from participating in the procurement) bids from suppliers who are constituted or organised under Russian or Belarusian law, or whose 'Persons of Significant Control' information indicates residency in Russia or Belarus, unless the supplier (or any member of their supply chain they rely on to deliver the contract):
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus
Overview

content_blocks.text: is registered in the UK or in a country the UK has a relevant international agreement with reciprocal rights of access to public procurement, and / or
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus
Overview

content_blocks.text: has significant business operations in the UK, or in a country the UK has relevant international agreements with reciprocal rights of access to public procurement.
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus
Overview

content_blocks.text: If either of the above criteria apply, the supplier should not be automatically excluded from a new procurement, as the non-discrimination, equal treatment and remedy provisions contained within the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (PCR 2015) apply.

content_blocks.text: take account of the fact that where the supplier (or any member of their supply chain they rely on to deliver the contract) meets certain criteria as outlined in the PPN, they should not be automatically excluded from the procurement, as the non-discrimination, equal treatment and remedy provisions contained within PCR 2015 apply
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus

content_blocks.text: consider the specific circumstances and take legal advice where appropriate, where the supplier has a more complex group structure involving parent or group companies based or operating in the UK, or in a country the UK has a relevant international agreement with reciprocal rights of access to procurement
heading_path: Contracts with suppliers from Russia and Belarus

content_blocks.text: conduct due diligence to check supplier details with Companies House and other open information sources, or seek verification directly from the supplier.
